question: Let \(N\) be the product of all the positive integer divisors of \(42.\) What is the units digit of \(N?\)
solution:
Pair each divisor with the divisor that makes its product \(42\).

Because \(42=2\cdot3\cdot7\), a divisor is formed by choosing whether to include each of these three primes. There are \(2^3=8\) divisors, and the following four pairs include all eight exactly once:
\[
(1,42),\qquad(2,21),\qquad(3,14),\qquad(6,7).
\]
Each pair has product \(42\), so
\[
N=(1\cdot42)(2\cdot21)(3\cdot14)(6\cdot7)=42^4.
\]
The units digit of a product depends only on the units digits of its factors. Thus \(42^4\) has the same units digit as \(2^4=16\).

The units digit is \(\boxed{6}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
